chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Basie's first trip and New York as home; Mildred Bailey reunion
summary: Collins met Basie in 1937, with guitarist Claude Williams, and musicians looked after each other; at the Golden Gate Ballroom Mildred Bailey rehired him for her dates.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: On his first trip to New York?

That was his first trip out of Kansas City, I think, with the band. And I thought of the guitarist's name. His name was Claude Williams. And he played a very fine violin also. I don't think he stayed with them too long because when they went to New York they got Freddy Greene, you know. But during this time, as I told you, I met Basie, and Basie's whole band. It was Joe Jones and Prez, and -- no, Harry didn't join them until later, when they went east. I think Buck was with them then.
But any way, I -- for the last time I'll say this. I was there. Very much so, you know.
So any way, when I went to New York it was just like going home, because all of the musicians -- we had a -- more of a rapport then. I mean, it was a different feeling.

They kind of looked out for eachother. So my not having any money really didn't make any difference. You know, when I went to New York, because I knew I didn't have anything to worry about. Like Freddy Green. When he would come to Chicago, Count would always tell me, John, come to New York. I said, Freddy, you know, I don't know anybody. He said, look, don't worry, you just come, we'll look out for you. You know. You can't get musicians to do that now. You know, they feel a little differently.

But I went to New York, as I said, and it was like going home. I never worried. I knew I was going to eat, I knew I was going play, and I had a place to sleep, you know, and that was it. So I -- how I started to recording with Mildred, I went to the Golden Gate Ballroom one night to hear Teddy Wilson's band, his new band. He had a marvelous band, and Mildred Bailey was there. And she saw me and was reunion. And I recorded -- I did all of her recording after that. It was always Teddy Wilson, Roy Eldridge, and myself. You know? So again, how can they forget me?
I don't know. Well, any way, Pat, it's a mean, old world.
